# Plan: fix(mcp) newline-delimited JSON stdio framing — Issue #28 / wf-2026-07-30-001 (fast)

## Root cause
`internal/mcp/server.go` frames JSON-RPC with the LSP base protocol
(`Content-Length: N\r\n\r\n<body>`). MCP stdio requires newline-delimited JSON.
Server cannot interoperate with any real MCP client.

## Change set (minimal, contract-preserving)
1. `internal/mcp/server.go`
   - `readFrame`: read one `\n`-terminated line, trim `\r\n`, skip blank lines,
     return the line as the frame body. On EOF with a trailing unterminated line,
     return that line then EOF on the next call.
   - `writeFrame`: `json.Marshal` (compact, single-line) + append `\n`, `w.Write`.
   - `EncodeMessage` (test helper): marshal + append `\n`.
   - `DecodeResponses` (test helper): keep delegating to new `readFrame`.
   - Remove now-unused `strconv`/`fmt` imports if the compiler flags them.
2. `scripts/smoke.sh` (MCP section, ~lines 57–97): send newline-delimited requests;
   parse stdout by splitting on `\n` and `json.loads` each non-empty line. Drop the
   Content-Length header checks.
3. Docs (contract-coupled): `specs/001-architecture.md:85` +
   `specs/001-architecture.zh-CN.md:84` → "newline-delimited JSON framing (MCP stdio)".
   `specs/013-security-hardening.md` §1 → reframe the frame-size cap for the
   line-based reader (defense intent unchanged; no longer keyed to Content-Length).

## Tests (TDD: RED → GREEN)
- NEW wire-format test: feed raw `{"jsonrpc":"2.0",...}\n` frames, assert responses
  are `\n`-terminated JSON with NO `Content-Length`; and that a malformed/non-JSON
  line is skipped without crashing, plus EOF-without-trailing-newline is handled.
- Existing server_test.go / server_new_tools_test.go use the helpers → pass unchanged.

## Out of scope (recorded follow-up)
- `structuredContent`/`outputSchema` migration (clean move to standard, no dual-write).
- `ping` support, tool annotations.

## Validation ladder
mcp package tests → `go build ./...` → `go vet ./...` → `go test ./... -count=1`
→ `./scripts/smoke.sh`.
